hints.title: Use the common first term
hints.body: Write the AP as 12, 12+d, 12+2d, … and the GP as 12, r2, r22, ….
hints.recap: Write term positions before forming equations about their sums.
hints.pitfall: The third AP term contains 2d; the third GP term contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Translate the two given sums into equations.

hints.title: Eliminate d
hints.body: The second-term equation gives d+r2=0. Substituting d=−r2 into the third-term equation gives 12−r+r22=18.
hints.recap: Eliminating the AP difference produces a quadratic in the GP ratio.

hints.title: Apply convergence before summing
hints.body: Solve the ratio quadratic and test each candidate against the convergence restriction. Then use the permitted ratio with the original first term.
hints.recap: An infinite geometric series converges only when the absolute value of its ratio is below one.
hints.pitfall: Retain the given first term when using the sum formula.
hints.pause: Find the valid ratio and calculate the sum to infinity.

recall.reminder: An infinite geometric series converges only when the absolute value of its ratio is below one.

solution:
The conditions on the second terms give 12+d+r2=12, so d=−r2. The third terms give 12+2d+r22=18. Substitution yields 12−r+r22=18.

Multiplying by 8 gives 4r2−8r+3=(2r−1)(2r−3)=0. Only r=12 satisfies the given convergence requirement |r|<1.

The sum is therefore 121−12=1, option G.
